title: Debugging stream of consciousness — technical, corrections, frustration
raw: okay so the bug is happening in the checkout flow specifically when the user has more than one shipping address saved and they try to switch between them so what happens is the state updates correctly i can see that in the redux devtools but then the ui doesn't re-render and i thought it was a memoization problem with react memo no wait use memo and i added the dependency array correctly or at least i think i did but then i realized the shipping address component is wrapped in a higher order component that does its own shouldComponentUpdate no wait it's a class component mixed in with functional components and that's probably the actual problem because the class component is blocking the re-render by returning false from shouldComponentUpdate when it probably shouldn't and i've tried passing the address id as a prop directly but that didn't work either and i'm starting to think the whole thing needs to be rewritten as a functional component with use reducer but that's like a two day job and we need this fixed today so maybe i can just force a re-render with a key prop on the shipping address component and see if that unblocks it temporarily
reference:
The bug is in the checkout flow when a user has multiple saved shipping addresses and tries to switch between them. The state updates correctly (visible in Redux DevTools) but the UI doesn't re-render.

I thought it was a `useMemo` memoization issue with the wrong dependency array, but the real problem is probably the class component wrapper. It's returning `false` from `shouldComponentUpdate` and blocking the re-render. Mixing class components with functional components in the same tree is causing the issue.

Passing the address ID as a direct prop didn't fix it. The proper fix is rewriting it as a functional component with `useReducer`, but that's a two-day job. Short-term fix: force a re-render by changing the `key` prop on the shipping address component.
